finding.producer_to_consumer: ShellMesh::new derives BendQuad points then keeps each bend only if topology::bending_weights returns Some. The function rejects minor-vector norm <1e-12 after constructing an orthonormal plane basis; this is an absolute area-like threshold and not restricted to exactly degenerate geometry.
finding.symbolic_example: For s=2^-22, let the hinge be (0,0,0)→(s,0,0) and wings (s/2,s/2,0),(s/2,-s/2,0). Each triangle has strictly positive area s²/4. The chosen first basis is the x axis, and the plane-basis tests have squared lengths s² and s²/4, both >1e-24. Each of the four signed minors has magnitude s²/2, so their norm is s²=2^-44 <1e-12 and returns None. With density 1024, each positive corner mass exceeds the separate 1e-12 kg inverse-mass cutoff; all raw coordinates/density are finite. No fixture or computation was executed.
finding.conditions: Approximately 0.24 micrometre hinge length, much smaller than ordinary garment scales; source-local mesh admission has no minimum scale. Actual supported asset scale and expected geometry-error policy need confirmation. This is not a reason to force a bend for truly collapsed or collinear geometry.
